Final categorization: OK  
(Justification: The paper is a non-review research article that explicitly implements national-scale spatial modeling of land use/land cover change (LUCC) across the entire territory of Mexico (1,907,382 km²). Its primary objective is to identify hotspots of LUCC under two distinct future scenarios—business-as-usual (BAU) and a pessimistic scenario—with quantitative comparisons of projected changes in land cover classes (e.g., agriculture expanding from 24.4% in 1993 to 30–34% by 2050). The study uses a spatially explicit LUCC model (Weights of Evidence + Markov transition matrices) driven by socioeconomic and biophysical variables, produces mapped projections for 2020, 2050, and 2080, and includes quantitative validation metrics such as figure of merit (94%), allocation/quantity disagreement, and inter-GCM agreement maps. All core inclusion criteria are met: national scale, primary focus on LULC prediction, ≥2 future scenarios with quantitative comparison, spatial modeling with accuracy metrics, and mapped outputs. No exclusion criteria apply.)
